children: Stocks are struggling for momentum despite a solid start to earnings season on Wall Street.
JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo and Citi all reported higher profits this morning, but their shares have been bouncing around in volatile morning trading.

Overall, trading and banking were better than a year earlier but failed to live up to the booming second quarter. Still, banks expressed cautious optimism about the U.S. economy, saying businesses and consumers are still spending and looking resilient.
Tech stocks are also on unsure footing. Comments by CXMT, one of China's biggest memory makers, sparked fears of Chinese competition. Micron and other U.S. memory stocks are slumping.
Oil prices are retreating, but Brent crude remains around $105 a barrel as tensions persist in the Middle East.
This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
